articleTitle: Migration from the private network to the private ISDN
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Examines how ISDN techniques can assist in the construction of national and international wide area networks, capable of supporting all forms of voice, data and image communication. To achieve this objective it is necessary to understand why and how business have constructed private networks to recognise what benefits they have provided and to examine their current and future functionality. Within this context it is relevant to examine which ISDN recommendations and standards are applicable in the private network domain. This is particularly appropriate with respect to D channel signalling systems and to the relationship between the UK de-facto standards of DPNSS and DASS and the future international standards embodied within Q.Sig and DSS1.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Private virtual networks: key considerations
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Private virtual networking enables private network transport and services to be provided using public network infrastructure. This offers the corporate customer the benefits of reduced costs, the availability of advanced services and the simplicity of obtaining all networking services from one source. Also, PVNs offer the public network operator advantages in terms of growth in network traffic through rapid deployment of new services and ease of incorporation of new customers. The paper briefly reviews these benefits and then describes some of the main aspects of private virtual networks (PVNs). in particular it looks in detail at the different types of PVN, the application of intelligent networking (IN) techniques to PVNs, and the signalling issues affecting PVNs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimization method for virtual private network design
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The virtual private network (VPN) design is a research project of the Swiss PTT and the University of Berne. The goal of this project is a software tool, which aids a consultant to configure cost-effective VPNs based on (multiple) services provided by a telecommunication company. The design of the tool is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An architecture for a broadband LAN
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The author presents a low cost LAN, AMNET (a multimedia network), designed to be suitable for supporting multimedia communications on cheap personal computers and to be simple to interface with telecommunication networks. The network services, node architecture, ring operation, service adaptors and network adaptors are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving the software architecture of private switching systems using object-oriented techniques
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The paper presents the hypothesis that in order to produce a software architecture for a system that maintains its integrity in the face of continuous systems design iterations, it must be based upon reusable, evolvable and combinable autonomous software components. A system architecture that is based upon this premise will enable the conceptualization and design of new system requirements in a flexible and modular fashion. It describes the object-oriented methodology and how it may be used to construct a system from reusable, autonomous software components that can be independently developed, evolved and provisioned within the target system. In order to evaluate object-oriented techniques and compare them with conventional function-oriented techniques, a prototype switching system has been built using these techniques. The results of these evaluations are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A methodology for fault management in heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The author looks qualitatively at some specific problems that arise in the management of heterogeneous networks and suggest how an OSI based approach could be employed to solve them. The approach is rather practical, first introducing real life problems that are encountered in heterogeneous networks and pointing out how solutions to these problems can be extended to generalized fault management applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-speed multimedia backbone LAN
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The authors present the architecture and functions of high-speed multimedia backbone LAN (HMB-LAN) referring to a product named LX-7400. They apply a Call-by-Call dynamic channel allocation method to the HMB-LAN in order to manage heavy traffic and support broadband services. Since the HMB-LAN channels are released upon end-to-end disconnect, the HMB-LAN channel resources are efficiently utilized. Some examples of circuit switching services are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The challenge of multimedia dialup conferencing
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The author discusses live multimedia telecommunications for teleconferencing. Starting with videophones the author details the aspects that go to make up multimedia, and finishes with multiparty teleconferencing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bringing application services and users together-the electronic mail example
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: More and more people are using electronic mail systems. However, virtually no efforts have been made to examine in how far services provided by these systems really meet the actual user requirements. As an initial step, a rough analysis of user demands is given. This is followed by a brief introduction to CCITT's X.400/X.500 recommendations, which will form the basis of all future multivendor mail systems. Services defined in these recommendations are matched against the idenitfied requirements. Finally, some useful enhancements of X.400/X.500 are proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An information-driven approach to network security
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Risk analysis must be used to help telecommunication managers to decide how much it is appropriate to spend on security countermeasures and where, within the network, this spending should be directed. Risk analysis is based on the concepts of threat, vulnerability, attack, risk and countermeasure. Structured risk analysis, a hybrid methodology developed by Hyperion Systems Limited in the UK, is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A real time learning control for broadband ISDN
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: In such integrated services networks, the grades of service (GOS) is classified into call level and cell level. To satisfy both GOSs in the ATM (asynchronous transfer mode) networks for BISDN, the learning approach seems to be suitable, because the precise characteristics of the source traffic are unknown and this approach can be adapted for such complex systems. The authors propose a learning control, using the method of potential functions to identify the system characteristics and to estimate the blocking probability for the call-level GOS. As for maintaining the GOS for cell level, in order to estimate the cell delay for the cell-level GOS, in real time, they propose the equivalent MMPP (Markov modulated Poisson process) method. A numerical example for a video/data system is also given to show the effectiveness of this learning control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband-the effects on the private networking market
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The modern telecommunications market is a maze of new technologies, regulatory and globalisation forces, fundamental costs changes, tariff uncertainties and other components to add to the de-stabilisation of what was once a fairly predictable market. The paper addresses all these changes and by doing so attempts to clarify the salient issues in understanding the complexity of the modern telecommunications market and how broadband networks can provide private and virtual private network solutions. The paper examines the following areas: general market forces; evolution of telecommunications market niches; development and demand for broadband services; emerging broadband technologies; and what they can and cannot offer the customer. Some general conclusions are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Connection oriented high speed MANs and LANs: a requirement for B-ISDN evolution
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The introduction of a connection-oriented (CO) service to high speed LANs and MANs is the prerequisite for a high quality of service (QOS) as well as an easy, efficient and robust interworking with ATM. Both aspects are essential in the long term evolution of the public broadband network. The characteristics of such a service and their implications on resource management and interworking are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast packet switching private networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Two important trends are currently being witnessed in the evolution of private networks: the adoption of fast packet switching or cell switching as the technology of choice for private backbone networks, and the rapid acceptance of frame relay as the interface for the interconnection of local area networks (LANs). The paper examines the reasons for these changes and focusses in particular on the powerful combination of frame relay implemented on a cell relay infrastructure. Further, it is postulated that frame relay will become the dominant mode of data communications in the 1990s supporting not only the interconnection of LANs but also more traditional forms of corporate traffic such as SNA and video.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radio access in corporate technology networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Examines the development of digital cordless technology, and compares the Digital European Cordless Telephone (DECT) system with that of the GSM. As the DECT is believed to feature above all in the office environment as part of a PABX or even as a fully cordless PABX, it is useful to compare it with the other candidate cordless telephone standards: the CEPT's CT1 and CT2.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordination of distributed user-defined resource sharing supported by an intelligent communication network
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The author puts forward a concept whereby commodity-type resource sharing should be supported by an 'intelligent' communication network. Each network station is equipped with a handler responsible for scheduling requests for resources and keeping track of current resource availability. The author points out that many media access control methods used in today's communication networks ensure or can be modified to ensure identical order of received transmissions at all network stations, which reduces the resource allocation problem to scheduling requests in a single queue. Four heuristic resource allocation algorithms have been presented along with some anti-starvation measures. Their simulative evaluation can be helpful in the design of an algorithm that, given the traffic conditions and the system configuration, best trades average request delay for a fair access to resources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of gateway performance with interconnected LANS
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The authors investigate the performance of gateways with interconnected LANs and in particular focus on how to detect the occurrance of congestion in networks when mixed traffic of voice and data are carried. In the first section they consider the active talker model for m talkers in the system. They present the distribution of cumulative probabilities of the number of active talkers in talkspurt. They then use this distribution as a measure of congestion in the network. In section 3, they present and discuss the gateway performance measured experimentally on their laboratory model of interconnected LANs. The concluding remarks of the paper including the suggestion of a flow control scheme based on a cumulative probability model is given in section 4.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated network management system for the private international networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The authors present the development of the integrated network management system for the private international network (P-INMS) that can meet the recent end-to-end network management needs under the globalised and complicated network environments, for instance, efficient operation of multi-vendor networks quick restoration of network failures, improvement of network quality, customer controlled reconfiguration and life cycle management. The way to success is to establish an effective architecture for the network management system, the framework of designing P-INMS is addressed. Analyzing current environments, classifying management information and studying how to process management information are key points.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A regional data communications network for British Gas, Scotland
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: In early 1991 British Gas plc, Scotland, identified a requirement for a high speed resilient inter-office data communications network throughout the region. The network would provide services for Regional Headquarters in Edinburgh, seven large office sites throughout Scotland, with potential additional connections to depots ad showrooms. The project started in June 1991 with a feasibility study, followed by outline design approval of a business case, procurement and implementation. The authors present in the form of a case study the business and technical requirements, the process in which these were met and what practical lessons can be drawn concerning the state of the art and the approach to similar projects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrating the computer and telecommunications
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Computers are being integrated with private telecommunications systems in an increasing number of ways. Using the concept of servers connected to different interfaces of PBX systems provides a wide range of added-value features and options. Computer supported telephony applications (CSTA) and wideband servers are highlighted as two areas which will impact substantially on future networks to provide new applications and services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structure of international corporate networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The quality of international leased circuits is measured. The measured quality is the basis for subjective evaluation of high-efficiency coded voice and for experimental investigation of the transmission parameters appropriate for inter-LAN file transfer. As an example a triangular international corporate network linking Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States, constructed using these results, is presented. The appropriate speech coding rates and one-link voice digital transit configuration, the most appropriate packet size for inter-LAN file transfer, and guidelines for future international corporate networks design are all proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Private and public ISDN-planning the wedding
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The paper assesses the potential evolutionary power of today's PBX designs and puts it in the perspective of the changing communication demands of the business community in the next 5 years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Speaker verification routines for ISDN and UPT access and security using artificial neural networks and time encoded speech (TES) data
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: An initial investigation into the use of time encoded speech (TES) fixed size, fixed dimension A-matrices as the input layer of a simple fast artificial neural network (FANN) configured to identify the acoustic output of ten cooperative male imposters each articulating twenty versions of the same phrase produced very favourable indications which led to the work described in the paper. It would appear that the TES data structures involved may be well matched to the demands of artificial neural network architectures when these are applied to some of the important time-sequence learning requirements inherent in the significant task of speaker verification. Such a combination may well enable these very powerful FANN analysis and classification tools to be applied to advantage to the spoken utterances of voice network users under realistic operational conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband communication in private networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: A system concept is presented which allows for a smooth evolution from ISPBX to broadband ISPBX. Only those applications are handled via ATM that appear to be reasonable, so the economical progress of ISDN is possible independently of the introduction of ATM. The concept for a distributed system presented here is realized in the Esprit project 2146 'DAMS'. The traffic performance of ATM systems has been researched within the Berkom project 'ATD Study', and the integration strategy in the subscriber area is being developed in the Race project R1011 'Business CPN'.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CityNet-fibre optic access for business customers
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The CityNet service was introduced in the autumn of 1989 for corporate business customers in Helsinki. The idea of the service is to provide first big corporate customers and then later all the main business centers with access to the Helsinki Telephone Company's (HTC) fibre optic network. The need for the service was obvious already in 1987 when the first big private fibre optic networks to interconnect corporate wide LANs were built. The dedicated multimode fibre optic cables were provided by the HTC. It soon turned out to be impractical to provide all the big customers with dedicated cables and varying assemblies of different multi-mode and single-mode fibres. CityNet was introduced to serve corporate customers in their need of interconnecting LANs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Moving into the light (telecommunication technologies)
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Discusses the requirements for moving telecommunication technologies into the light of business benefits. Voice, data, text, image and video communication present a considerable challenge in bandwidth provision and management. The emergence of true international networks for both voice and data, and the arrival of by-pass opportunities should stimulate more responsive and user friendly PTOs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of a connectionless service in a wide area ATM network
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Proposes a CSMA with n collision permission (CSMA/NCP) system for accommodating CSMA/CD terminals to a wide area ATM network. CSMA/NCP includes two main algorithms. One is access control, in which for purposes of congestion control, adapters do not send any cells while they are receiving cells. The other is a strategy for maintaining the network quality, in which adapters use an ATM path at 1/n speed of the user network interface (UNI). The system throughput and packet loss rate are estimated. The results indicate that the throughput is high and packet loss rate is low and CSMA/NCP is useful, regardless of how long the distances between terminals are. The authors also demonstrate a way in which the most suitable collision permission number can be determined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hybrid packet switching techniques for multichannel integrated packet radio networks
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The integration of voice and data traffic in a multichannel private mobile radio network can be facilitated by hybrid packet switching techniques. An integrated system allows for adaptation to the variations in voice and data traffic load that occur in practice. It is shown that appropriate switching, queueing and transmission mechanisms can appreciably improve the packet traffic performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The business communications network management challenge
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The author describes the Alcatel Business Communications (ABC) solution to network management. It provides a network architecture, network management architecture, related protocols and the A 8050 network management centre. The services follow the OSI categorisation, providing management of: faults, configuration, domain, performance, security and accounting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cryptographic security techniques for digital mobile telephones
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: Deals with various generic aspects concerning the application of cryptographic techniques to digital cordless and cellular telephone systems. The work presented is based on a review of literature regarding the relevant standards and recommendations for current and future systems. Particular reference is made to the ETSI GSM system. The aspects discussed include the choice of cryptographic algorithm, including public key cryptography, and the choice of protocols for such functions as cryptographic key management and user authentication. Various conclusions are drawn regarding the choice of the above, these being summarised by four key recommendations for current and future system design. The paper is concluded with a proposal for future research into the development of new security techniques for current and future systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Private networks-the technology evolution to support customer demands
publicationTitle: 1992 Second International Conference on Private Switching Systems and Networks
abstract: The paper considers the technology evolutions that are necessary to meet the needs of customers' private communications. It considers: the evolution of business requirements covering the development of international businesses and the need to extend the network communications; the means by which the requirements for small business locations, currently excluded from full private network participation on a cost basis, will be incorporated into the private network by reducing the end user costs for service provision; and the mechanisms by which the public network centrex service provision will be used to complement the private network allowing effective homeworking and fully distributed offices. It also examines how the technologies relating to network services such as mobility, video communications and wideband data will impact the creation and use of private networks; and how the telecommunications regulations of the UK and especially Europe will have to be modified to allow the full realisation of the potentials enabled by the technologies developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
